Don't buy Kalyan Jewellers before you see this. One shop in Thrissur became five hundred and forty six. Multibagger, or trap? Part one.
It began in 1993, in Kerala. Now, three hundred sixty five Kalyan showrooms in India, thirty eight in the Middle East, two in the US, two in the UK, and one hundred thirty eight Candere stores.
Sales went from nine thousand seven hundred crore in FY19 to thirty five thousand seven hundred crore in FY26. Almost four times.
Profit went from a loss in FY21 to one thousand three hundred fifty crore in FY26. And three hundred forty nine crore in just the June quarter.
Last quarter, revenue grew twenty six percent, and same store sales grew twenty percent. Old showrooms are selling more, not just new ones.
The IPO came at eighty seven rupees in 2021, and listed fifteen percent lower. Today it closed at five hundred sixty. So who owns it now?
Promoters hold almost sixty three percent. Shareholders jumped from three point seven lakh to six point seven lakh. But foreign investors cut their stake from twenty six percent to under fourteen.
The catch? It trades at about forty times earnings. It carries over six thousand crore of borrowings, mostly gold loans. And it lives and dies by gold demand.
Save this, and send it to your Kalyan Jewellers group. Not a buy or sell call. Follow money in cloud for part two.
